title: Unbounded closed projection with arbitrary etale ring sheaves
statement:
Let i:Z→T be a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion], and j:U→T its complementary open immersion; use the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let R be any sheaf of commutative rings on T, and RZ its actual inverse image on Z. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let iStar be any additive left adjoint to actual sectionwise module direct image, and let iPull,iPush be functors identified with their termwise complex functors by natural Q-factorization isomorphisms. For any normalized ringed-site duality models t on (T,R) and z on (Z,RZ) [def-zl-ringed-site-duality-model], there is an isomorphism of bifunctors on D(Z)×D(T), natural in both variables:

 iPush(N tensor_z iPull(K)) ≅ iPush(N) tensor_t K.

There is no exceptional adjoint, dualizing object, boundedness, constructibility or Tor-amplitude condition in this statement.

source.place: Middle projection identity, expanded by closed counit and open-closed detection

proof.text: For a closed immersion, IsFinite is automatic. Apply the already proved finite etale direct-image exactness [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] with AddCommGrpCat coefficients. The actual module pushforward followed by forgetting its coefficient action is definitionally the source module forgetful functor followed by this abelian-sheaf direct image. Module forgetful functors preserve finite colimits [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] and reflect them, since they preserve colimits and reflect isomorphisms. Thus the actual module pushforward preserves finite colimits. This entire coefficient-action argument is Lean-proved in the private closedEtaleModulePushExact helper, for an arbitrary coefficient map. The closed counit and supported essential image are [lem-kun-04ca]; they give j^{-1}i_*=0 and joint detection by i^{-1},j^{-1}. Indeed if j^{-1}F=0, its support is in Z, so F≅i_*G and i^{-1}F≅G; if the latter is zero, so is F. These abelian-sheaf assertions apply to module sheaves: the canonical maps respect the induced coefficient actions, and forgetting those actions reflects isomorphisms.

The inverse-image functors on abelian sheaves are exact by
[lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]. For the identified coefficient
sheaves, module pullback is inverse image: the tensor formula in
[lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] has inverse maps
$m\otimes a\mapsto am$ and $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. Thus module inverse image
is exact as well. Exactness of both $i^{-1}$ and $i_*$ lets their termwise
functors, unit, and counit descend through the localization at
quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; the homotopy
adjunction and its triangle identities are
[lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. Hence
$i^{-1}\dashv Ri_*=i_*$ on the ordinary derived categories, and the closed
counit stays invertible. Since exact inverse image commutes with cohomology,
the joint detection in step 1 also detects acyclic complexes, by applying it
to every cohomology sheaf.
For $t=i,j$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] gives
$t^{-1}(P\otimes^L Q)\cong t^{-1}P\otimes^Lt^{-1}Q$ for arbitrary complexes,
with the relevant inverse-image coefficient rings; no Tor bound is used. The given Q-factorizations identify all the allowed presentations with these localized functors. The K-flat comparisons in [def-zl-ringed-site-duality-model] identify the derived tensor comparisons with the tensor functors of the two supplied normalized models.

For arbitrary $N\in\mathcal D(Z)$ and $K\in\mathcal D(T)$, form the
projection morphism
$$c_{N,K}:i_*N\otimes^L K\longrightarrow i_*(N\otimes^Li^{-1}K)$$
as the adjoint, under step 2, of
$i^{-1}(i_*N\otimes^LK)\cong i^{-1}i_*N\otimes^Li^{-1}K
\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_N\otimes1}N\otimes^Li^{-1}K$.
Applying $i^{-1}$ to $c_{N,K}$ gives this isomorphism followed by the inverse
closed counit, so is invertible. Applying $j^{-1}$ gives the map between
zero objects, since $j^{-1}i_*=0$ and inverse image commutes with derived
tensor. Exact inverse image preserves mapping cones, since the termwise additive
functor preserves their direct sums and differential matrices. The cone of
$c_{N,K}$ therefore has both inverse images acyclic and is acyclic by
step 2. The morphism from the zero object to this cone induces an
isomorphism on every cohomology sheaf, hence is an isomorphism by
[lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology]. The cone is a zero object,
so [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] makes $c_{N,K}$ an isomorphism.
The construction is natural in $N,K$. Inverting this natural projection map gives i_*(N tensor i^*K) ≅ i_*N tensor K, the orientation of the Lean conclusion. Both variables remain arbitrary in the ordinary unbounded derived categories; the zero and empty-complement cases use the same zero-object argument.

lean.statement:
theorem closedImmersionEtaleProjection
    {T Z U : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ T) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (j : U ⟶ T) [IsOpenImmersion j]
    (hij : Set.range j.base = (Set.range i.base)ᶜ)
    (R : Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology CommRingCat.{u + 1}) :
    let RZ := (Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback
      (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ i) CommRingCat.{u + 1}
      (T.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale) (Z.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)).obj R
    let MT := ringedSiteModules.{u + 1} ((sheafCompose T.smallEtaleTopology
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj R)
    let MZ := ringedSiteModules.{u + 1} ((sheafCompose Z.smallEtaleTopology
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj RZ)
    letI : HasDerivedCategory.{u + 2} MT := HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    letI : HasDerivedCategory.{u + 2} MZ := HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    let V₀ : MZ ⥤ MT :=
      SheafOfModules.pushforward.{u + 1}
      (F := MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ i)
      (J := T.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale) (K := Z.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)
      (S := (sheafCompose T.smallEtaleTopology
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj R)
      (R := (sheafCompose Z.smallEtaleTopology
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj
      ((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback
      (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ i) CommRingCat.{u + 1}
      (T.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale) (Z.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)).obj R))
      ⟨Functor.whiskerRight ((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafAdjunctionContinuous
      (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ i) CommRingCat.{u + 1}
      (T.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale) (Z.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)).unit.app R).hom
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})⟩
    letI : V₀.Additive := ⟨by intros; rfl⟩
    ∀ (iStar : MT ⥤ MZ) [iStar.Additive] (ai : iStar ⊣ V₀)
      (iPull : DerivedCategory MT ⥤ DerivedCategory MZ)
      (pullFactors : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ iPull ≅
        iStar.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
      (iPush : DerivedCategory MZ ⥤ DerivedCategory MT)
      (pushFactors : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ iPush ≅
        V₀.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
      (t : RingedSiteDualityModel.{u + 1, u, 0, u + 2} T.smallEtaleTopology R)
      (z : RingedSiteDualityModel.{u + 1, u, 0, u + 2} Z.smallEtaleTopology RZ),
      Nonempty (((𝟭 (DerivedCategory MZ)).prod iPull) ⋙ z.closed.tensor ⋙ iPush ≅
        (iPush.prod (𝟭 (DerivedCategory MT))) ⋙ t.closed.tensor)

split_report.summary: Separate the actual closed projection formula, without exceptional inverse image or a dualizing object, from the Hom-chain and Yoneda argument.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes only the middle projection identity of closed-costalk duality.

tool_uses.why: Use only the generic small-etale exact fully faithful closed pushforward and supported essential image, as already used in the parent projection argument.

Use only the existing exact finite etale direct-image instance with abelian-group coefficients, for the closed immersion. The coefficient-action reflection bridge is proved privately here; no cohomological-dimension or curve-unit conclusion is invoked.
Use only the generic exact forgetful functor from module sheaves to abelian sheaves. The source sheafification API supplies the finite-colimit-preserving instance used in the private exactness proof.
